items.name: A. Lange & Söhne
items.summary: Founder of the Glashütte watchmaking tradition. Nationalised after WWII, the brand was refounded in 1990 by Walter Lange and Günter Blümlein and is renowned for German silver plates, hand-engraved balance cocks and the outsized date.

items.name: Apple
items.summary: Apple launched the Apple Watch in 2015. Within a few years it became the best-selling watch in the world by unit volume, mainstreaming health sensors such as ECG and blood-oxygen measurement on the wrist.

items.name: Audemars Piguet
items.summary: Based in the Vallée de Joux, Audemars Piguet launched the Royal Oak in 1972, the Gérald Genta design that created the luxury steel sports watch category.

items.name: Breitling
items.summary: Breitling is closely tied to aviation and chronographs. Its Navitimer (1952) carries a slide-rule bezel for flight calculations, and the brand helped develop the separate start/stop and reset pushers of the modern chronograph.

items.name: Cartier
items.summary: The Paris jeweller created one of the first purpose-built men's wristwatches, the Santos (1904), for aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont, and the Tank (1917). Cartier defines shaped, design-led watches.

items.name: Casio
items.summary: Casio entered watches with the Casiotron in 1974 and changed the industry with the shock-resistant G-Shock in 1983. Its affordable digital watches, like the F-91W, are among the best-selling watches ever made.

items.name: Citizen
items.summary: Citizen is one of the largest movement makers in the world (through Miyota) and the pioneer of light-powered Eco-Drive watches. It also owns brands such as Bulova, Frédérique Constant and Arnold & Son.

items.name: Garmin
items.summary: A GPS specialist, Garmin builds multisport and outdoor smartwatches with long battery life, deep training metrics and navigation features favoured by athletes and adventurers.

items.name: Grand Seiko
items.summary: Created in 1960 to rival the best Swiss watches, Grand Seiko became an independent brand in 2017. It is celebrated for Zaratsu polishing, nature-inspired dials and three distinct technologies: Hi-Beat mechanical, 9F quartz and Spring Drive.

items.name: Hamilton
items.summary: Founded in Pennsylvania, Hamilton supplied railroad and military watches, launched the first battery-powered watch (Electric 500, 1957) and the first LED digital watch, Pulsar. It is now Swiss-based and famous for field watches and film appearances.

items.name: HMT
items.summary: HMT ("the Time Keepers of the Nation") produced India's first domestically made wristwatches, beginning in collaboration with Citizen. Its hand-wound Janata and Pilot models are cult collectibles; the watch division largely ceased production in 2016.

items.name: IWC Schaffhausen
items.summary: Founded by an American engineer in German-speaking Switzerland, IWC is known for pilot's watches, the Portugieser and robust engineering such as the Pellaton winding system.

items.name: Jaeger-LeCoultre
items.summary: Known as "the watchmaker's watchmaker", JLC has produced well over a thousand calibres and supplied movements to many great houses. Its Reverso (1931) has a case that flips to protect the crystal.

items.name: Longines
items.summary: Longines has a long history in aviation and sports timing, and its winged hourglass logo is one of the oldest registered trademarks still in use. It is known for classic, heritage-inspired designs.

items.name: NOMOS Glashütte
items.summary: Founded weeks after the fall of the Berlin Wall, NOMOS is known for Bauhaus-inspired design and in-house movements, including its own escapement ("swing system"), at comparatively accessible prices.

items.name: Omega
items.summary: Omega began as Louis Brandt's workshop in La Chaux-de-Fonds. Its Speedmaster went to the Moon in 1969 and its co-axial escapement and METAS Master Chronometer certification set modern benchmarks for accuracy and anti-magnetism.

items.name: Orient
items.summary: Orient is a favourite for first mechanical watches, producing its own automatic movements at very low prices. It has been fully part of Seiko Epson since 2009.

items.name: Patek Philippe
items.summary: One of the oldest continuously operating manufactures, Patek Philippe is synonymous with grand complications, perpetual calendars and record-breaking auction results. It is still family-owned.

items.name: Rolex
items.summary: Founded in London and moved to Geneva, Rolex pioneered the waterproof Oyster case (1926) and the Perpetual rotor (1931). Today it is the most recognised luxury watch brand in the world, known for robust in-house movements and tool-watch icons.

items.name: Seiko
items.summary: Seiko launched the world's first quartz wristwatch, the Astron, in 1969, and is one of the very few makers that produces nearly every component in-house. Its range runs from entry-level automatics to high-end Prospex and Presage pieces.

items.name: Sinn
items.summary: Sinn makes rugged tool watches for pilots, divers and specialist units, with technologies like Tegiment surface hardening, Ar-dehumidifying capsules and magnetic-field protection.

items.name: TAG Heuer
items.summary: Heuer was a pioneer of stopwatches and racing chronographs, co-developing one of the first automatic chronograph movements (Calibre 11) in 1969. It became TAG Heuer in 1985.

items.name: Timex
items.summary: Descended from the Waterbury Clock Company, Timex democratised the wristwatch with affordable, durable pieces ("takes a licking and keeps on ticking") and introduced the Indiglo backlight in 1992.

items.name: Tissot
items.summary: Tissot offers Swiss-made watches at accessible prices. Its PRX revived the 1970s integrated-bracelet look, and its Powermatic 80 movement offers an 80-hour power reserve at entry price points.

items.name: Tudor
items.summary: Created by Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf as a more accessible sister brand. Since the 2010s, Tudor has built a strong identity with the Black Bay family and its own in-house manufacture calibres.
